Engine assigns Sasih Ketiga (idx 3) to 2026-09-01..09 and Sasih Kapat (idx 4) to 2026-09-10..15. kalenderbali.info September 2026 calendar assigns Sasih Kapat (idx 4) to 2026-09-01..09 and Sasih Katiga (idx 3) to 2026-09-10..15. Both sources agree on the boundary day (2026-09-09/10) and on Saka year (1948). The names on either side of the boundary are swapped between the two sources. Off-by-one in Sasih indexing. Likely related to internal/external year-number inconsistency in saka.py: the externally-exposed saka_year is computed via `gregorian_year - 1978` while the sasih loop iterates `SAKA_EPOCH_YEAR + year_offset` starting at 1901 (off by one). Resolving this without authority validation would be unsafe.

Engine returns Triwara Kajeng for 2026-09-01; kalenderbali.info returns Beteng. The pattern across 2026-09-01..09 is `engine_tri = (ref_tri + 1) mod 3`. The Triwara cycle starts one day later in the engine than in the reference. Consistent 1-day offset across multiple dates suggests a single root cause (likely same as the Sasih dispute). Need to verify if a single epoch correction resolves both.

Engine uses 'Keliwon' for pancawara idx 4; kalenderbali.info uses 'Kliwon'. Both spellings are valid in Balinese; the engine spelling is more common in modern Bali. No arithmetic impact, only labeling. Standardize on 'Kliwon' (matches kalenderbali.info and the spelling used in many Balinese-English glossaries). Update i18n.py.
